summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later question answering; the source text itself is not needed)

## BOOK 1 of 2: The Sea Mystery (Freeman Wills Crofts; Inspector Joseph French, C.I.D., Scotland Yard)

**Characters:** Mr. Morgan (manager, tin-plate works, Burry Port; small, clean-shaven, baggy Norfolk suit); Evan Morgan (14, his son, at school; going back to school the next day); Sergeant Nield (Burry Port police; cultivated; efficient); Constables Williames, Smith, Watson; Coastguard Tom Manners (ex-Royal Navy, from Shoreditch; small, stout, elderly); Superintendent Griffiths (Llanelly); Major Lloyd (Chief Constable, Llandilo); Dr. Crowth (local police surgeon, bluff, middle-aged); Dr. Wilbraham (Lloyd's friend); Inspector French (short, stout, keen blue eyes, twinkle; "pleasant, friendly" method); Superintendent Howells (Swansea); Mr. Llewellyn (Fisher Street garage, Swansea); Mr. Evans (junior clerk, goods office, Morriston Road); Sergeant Jefferies; Constable David Jenkins (Neath); Sergeant Daw (Ashburton); Mr. Berlyn (Charles Berlyn, junior partner Veda Works, fair/red-haired, blue eyes, high colour); Stanley Pyke (engineer/travelling rep, dark, sallow, brown eyes); Mrs. Phyllis Berlyn; Colonel Domlio (senior partner/owner, lives at "Torview"? on moor, 3/4 mile from road, entomologist); Mr. Fogden (sales manager, Veda Works); Puddicoombe (packer); Gurney (night watchman, goatee, wizened; wife); Peter Small (fireman); Mr. Makepeace (garage, Ashburton); Mr. Illingworth (Ardlo Magneto Co.); Mrs. Billing (Pyke's landlady, Ashburton, East Street); Lizzie Johnston (Berlyns' maid); Peter Swann (gardener); Jefferson Pyke (cousin, Argentine rancher; real one dies at Nice); Mrs. Welsh (landlady, Kepple Street, London); Vera Welsh (her daughter, typist); Mr. Cooke; Ganope (tobacconist, Oakley Street); John Burt and Sarah Burt (Domlio's servants); Coombe (chauffeur); Mee (gardener); Alf Beer (Lizzie's fiancé); Dr. Lancaster; Mr. Tarkington (Hellifield? no – Burry story: n/a). Mr. Morgan's name etc.

**Plot in order:**
1. Late Sept, Burry Inlet. Morgan & Evan fishing; line snags a large crate ~20 ft down; grapnel hooks it; they tow it to Burry Port lifeboat slip. Morgan opens it: decomposing man in underclothes, face battered. Sergeant Nield, Manners, Chief Constable Lloyd, Dr. Crowth & Dr. Wilbraham examine. Dead 5–6 weeks; cause: blow to back of head, face smashed after death. Birthmark: small triangular, back of left arm. Crate: 3 ft x 2 ft 3 in x 2 ft 4 in, spruce, label torn off, steel bar ~14 in weight. Inquest adjourned 3 weeks. Lloyd calls Scotland Yard.
2. French arrives; examines body; sketch of birthmark; notes 14 nail holes (7 at each of two diagonal corners) → theorises crate floated, sinking after water leaked in. Calculations (Molesworth): crate 406 lb w/ contents, displacement 985 lb, buoyancy 579 lb; ~1 hour to sink. Pencil test: holes just under 1/6 in.
3. Experiment with Manners on tide tables: Loughor road bridge (ebb, ~1–2 hrs after HW; dates 21–23 Aug). Next day experiment: crate thrown from Loughor bridge 9:30; sank after 1 hr 7 min near original spot.
4. Lorry: crane-lorry seen at Neath (Constable David Jenkins), Gorseinon, Morriston; hired from Llewellyn's, Swansea, by "John F. Stewart" (letter from St. Pancras Hotel, typed); driver red-haired, glasses, stout. Crate loaded at Morriston Road Goods Station (Swansea), addressed to "James S. Stephenson", from Veda Office Equipment Mfg Co., Ashburton, South Devon (duplicator order dated 12 Aug, from Euston Hotel).
5. Ashburton: Veda crate packed night 15 Aug; night watchman Gurney; Berlyn & Pyke vanished 15 Aug night on Dartmoor after car breakdown (magneto short); Mrs Berlyn's maid; Sergeant Daw. French's tests: car breakdown, time-table, watchman, duplicator removal. Discovers Burry Port body's clothes match Pyke (Mrs Billing identifies darned grey sock, buttons, cuff-links). Jefferson Pyke (cousin) identifies birthmark; London address 17b Kepple Street.
6. Mrs Berlyn interviewed (Park Walk, Chelsea). Ardlo: magneto can be shorted and swapped; spare magneto ordered by "Henry Armstrong" (Westcliff Hotel, Bristol). Duplicator & crate faked records; Gurney's tea drugged; Lizzie's fiancé Alf Beer's story: overheard Pyke & Mrs Berlyn plotting ("I tell you 'e knows").
7. Domlio interviewed; Burt & wife (Mrs Burt saw Domlio return ~2 am). Domlio's false statement (lost locket; photo blackmail letter "X.Y.Z."). Parts found in well at Torview; Pyke's clothes found in well. Domlio cleared; Mrs Berlyn's "accident" at Upper Merton glen.
8. Mrs Berlyn's alibi (party); Hampstead Heath meeting; Pyke/Mrs Berlyn discussed "confess" plan; escape by roof from Kepple Street; Victory Place flat (Elephant & Castle), Perrin flat No. 19. French nearly shot; struggle; Mrs Berlyn chokes French; Carter rescues.
9. Conclusion: Stanley Pyke impersonated Jefferson (false heels, padding, rubber cheek discs, glasses); real Jefferson died at Nice of appendicitis (Pyke had hotel basin trick at Houston). Berlyn murdered by Pyke (sandbag) on return from Tavistock, 15 Aug; Phyllis drugged Gurney, changed magneto, footprints in Berlyn's shoes; Pyke rode her bicycle to Domlio's, dropped clothes in well, pawned bicycle at Plymouth (Tue 16 Aug). Both Pyke and Phyllis hanged ("Some three weeks after the next assizes ... paid for their crime with their lives"). Escape flat in Victory Place. Ganope relayed messages. Notes: Mrs Billing; Ruth? n/a.

## BOOK 2 of 2: The Starvel Hollow Tragedy (Freeman Wills Crofts; Inspector French)

**Characters:** Ruth Averill (20, orphan, dark, small; niece of miser Simon Averill of Starvel House, Starvel Hollow, Yorkshire moors near Thirsby; born in Southern France, father Theodore Averill, mother Anne de Condillac; Biarritz/Bayonne); Simon Averill (miser; safe full of notes & gold; invalid); John Roper (attendant/manservant; squint; formerly at Ransome Institute, Kintilloch, Fife; drunk claimed; blackmailer; forger); Flora Roper (née Macfarlane; wife; former maid of Mrs Philpot); Markham Giles (entomologist, ex-soldier, cottage half mile away; died of cocaine injection); Pierce Whymper (junior architect, Leeds, Nixon & Arbuthnot; clerk of works at Thirsby church; lodger 12 Stanhope Terrace; Oaklands, Bolton Road, Leeds); Mrs Oxley & Arthur Oxley (solicitor); Chief Constable Major Valentine (Leeds); Sergeant Kent (Thirsby police; bungler); Dr. Emerson (old, certificate); Dr. Herbert Philpot (Thirsby; Kintilloch assistant; gambler; forged confession; wife Edna Menzies killed May 1921; nurse Williams); Tarkington (bank manager, Northern Shires Bank; "hawk-like"); Bloxham (clerk); Mr. Mitchell (Chief Inspector, Yard); Inspector Willis; Inspector Tanner; Mrs Palmer-Gore (York, Oakdene, Ashton Drive; invitation to Ruth); Judith Carr (barmaid); George Mellowes (farmer; saw drunk Roper); Constable Sheldrake; Mrs Billing? (no, that's book 1). Colonel Followes (magistrate); Dr. Lingard (Hellifield police surgeon); Dr. Laming (Home Office); Mr. Simkins (undertaker); Abel Hesketh (town officer); Peter Spence (breadcart driver); Mrs Eliza Steele; Miss Locke sisters; Stokes (tramp); Mr. Stephenson (safe makers, Carter & Stephenson, Leeds; safe no. 12,473); MacGregor (Kintilloch sergeant); Dr. Ferguson; Mr. Pullar (shoe shop); Mr. Alderdice (jeweller); Stanley (salesman); Mr. Russell; Dashwood & Munce (stockbrokers, Gracechurch St, Dover House); Mr. Arthur Lisle Whitman (Roper alias); Macdonald (tobacconist, Moray St, Edinburgh); Sergeant Elliott; Carlton; Peveril Hotel (Russell Sq); Strand Palace; Peebles (Roper's mother, huckster); Mrs MacIntosh (Kilgore St, Glasgow).

**Plot in order:**
1. Sept 15 (Wed) 1926 fire at Starvel; Ruth away in York (Mrs Palmer-Gore invited her via forged note; "Oakdene"; £10 from uncle via Roper). Giles ill; died Tuesday (14 Sep). Three bodies: Averill (south wing), Ropers (NW). Oxley telegram. Sergeant Kent. Inquest: verdict fire, cause unknown; coroner Dr. Lonsdale; Roper drunk per Judith Carr & Mellowes.
2. Ruth inherits; Oxley plans her investment; Mrs Oxley. Tarkington notices 20-pound note (from £320 sent by Bloxham, 16 twenties) paid in in London ~18 Oct; suspects burglary. Chief Constable Valentine.
3. French assigned (Chief Inspector Mitchell). Safe fireproof (Carter & Stephenson). Burnt ash = newspapers (Leeds Mercury 13–15 Sep; "RAT-CATCHER'S FATAL FALL"). Notes removed, newspapers burned, door shut.
4. Tarkington list of 193 twenties (11 consignments). Bank note traced to Cook's, Regent St; £480 in Whymper's desk (24 twenties; 25 sent, one used). Whymper: Averill sent him 6 Oct payment £16 8s 4d for Talloires trip. Whymper story: Roper gave him £500 to go to Talloires for "Prosper Giraud" / "Mme Madeleine Blancquart"; Theodore Averill alias. French checks: Biarritz records (married 24 Jun 1905; Ruth b. 17 Jul 1906 d. mother; baptised 19 Aug 1906; father d. 8 Sep 1910). Whymper's story was Roper's invention.
5. Philpot: confession (15 May 1921, Kintilloch) forged; Edna Philpot death on stairs. Roper blackmail. Confirms forgery (upside-down copy). Philpot in debt, leaves for Glasgow (Mrs MacIntosh, Kilgore St). Dr. Emerson's myocarditis certificate on Giles.
6. Mrs Palmer-Gore: invitation letter forged (Averill never wrote). Ruth didn't know of the flower show.
7. Giles exhumed: coffin empty but half-full of earth. Mitchell/valentine. French's cumulative reasoning. Yellow clay near Starvel; French digs; body of Giles found wrapped in blanket buried on moor near Starvel (shed handcart). Post-mortem: cocaine injection (Dr. Lingard). Dr. Emerson admits error.
8. Trap at inquest: French's fabricated story; wedding-ring theory (Tower Bridge, lighter Fickle Jane; skipper James Gray, crew William Fuller; 39 gold 18-ct rings on cord). Jewellers' circular; shop at Stanley's (thick false moustache, tinted glasses, Homburg; £20 note change, 35 shillings). Roper identified (ring purchases, Carlton lunch, Peveril Hotel register "Jas. Fulton, Manchester", cut thumb).
9. Dashwood & Munce: Whitman invested ~£2000 Brazilian stock; address Macdonald, Edinburgh. Telegram to Whitman: meet Munce at Waverley 6:15 pm Tuesday. Tanner impersonates Munce. Philpot (brought from Glasgow) aids identification of thumb cut.
10. Waverley: Philpot pulls Mills bomb; struggle; Tanner disarms. Philpot's full confession: killed Edna with trip-cord; Roper & Flora witnessed; Philpot's plan: murder Averill, Ropers, Giles (cocaine); Roper stabbed by Philpot. Money recovered: cashbox, total £36,562. Philpot hanged. Ruth marries Pierce Whymper.
